status: Unreleased native QuickJS repeated-entry support. Public contexts admission, execution integration and durable exclusive ownership remain open. Published SDK/runtime and production remain 0.19.2.

behavior.entry: Reusing a known logical entry path creates a fresh native ESM identity and executes its newly supplied source. Generation is bounded, checked for overflow and skips identities occupied by user modules.
behavior.metadata: The original logical filePath supplies import.meta.filename and URL-encoded import.meta.url. Native identities may be up to 8 KiB so a 4 KiB filename is not truncated by the private generation suffix. Filesystem input paths retain their 4 KiB bound.
behavior.imports: Canonical imported modules retain identity and state. Static and dynamic imports of the same canonical path use the same cached module, including a canonical import of a previously executed entry.
behavior.retainedFunctions: Each module metadata helper closes over its owning native identity. A function retained from an earlier entry keeps that entry import cache, even when a new execution reuses the logical filename.
behavior.compiler: The compiled dynamic-import calling convention is unchanged. The owning loader binds the native identity while accepting the existing compiled base argument. Ordinary canonical-module records retain their existing encoding; generated retained entries carry their logical filePath in the owning Program Schema.
behavior.sourceCapture: ModuleSource owns optional logical filePath metadata for a generated entry identity. Ordinary canonical modules use their own name and omit that field. Captured source graphs retain generated identities and logical metadata, with the same total 128-module and 8 MiB bounds.
behavior.admission: Changed non-entry cached module sources and non-quiescent execution remain rejected. Failed graph validation leaves the prior registry and output intact.

checks.result: 12 passed and one obsolete assertion failed: it required reused entry rejection. The test now requires successful same-entry reexecution with fresh output and the incremented retained closure.

18 tests passed, 0 failed in 0.03 seconds. Covers repeated source/filename/URL, Unicode and reserved characters, retained dynamic-import closures, canonical static/dynamic cache equality, 4 KiB filename, collision avoidance and transactional graph-budget rejection.
Build, SDK build, TypeScript, Clippy with warnings denied, all workspace Rust tests and native Alchemy workerd tests passed. Bun: 417 pass, 0 fail, 5987 assertions across 92 files in 238.78 seconds.
Oxfmt, cargo fmt and Rust fixture formatting passed.

replacementProof.transport: Native Alchemy workerd and real R2 pages; each previous Worker is fully closed before replacement.
replacementProof.worker1: Retains a lexical variable and a closure, then parks on an echo callback.
replacementProof.worker2: Completes the first operation with result 43, then executes new source at the same logical path. The retained closure returns 42; output contains only second/closure and metadata remains file:///tmp/repeated.js.
replacementProof.worker3: Restores the second paged heap and executes another new source at the same path. The retained closure returns 43, the explicit round marker is third and filename/URL remain unchanged.
replacementProof.persistence: Pages are content addressed, validated before native adoption and uploaded only for newly encountered hashes. Native R2 calls and inventories are checked by the fixture.

limits: This is native local proof; no new release, deployment or production context API is claimed.
Full Node/package resolution, execution options and retained Python globals remain open.
Public context lifecycle operations, scoped authority, exclusive ownership and interrupted-operation settlement remain open.
Runtime heaps require an exact binary digest; cross-build heap migration remains unsupported.
No production latency, throughput, billing or total-parity claim follows from these tests.
